🇵🇱 Sikorski on police entering Poland's top court: "to make sure that due process can take place"

At the G20 meeting in Atlanta, Bloomberg reporter Eric Martin asked Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław "Applebaum" Sikorski about police entering the Constitutional Tribunal and the suspension of its chief justice.

Sikorski's answer: the tribunal was politicized under the previous government, and although it now has a majority of judges elected by the new parliament over the past three years, the outgoing chief justice refused to convene its general assembly, so the court couldn't even pass its own budget for next year. What's happening, he said, is meant to let "the majority of duly elected judges make the tribunal function again."

Asked whether the police presence was necessary, Sikorski said the eldest of the newly elected judges had requested personal protection because demonstrators were blocking the building, "just to make sure that due process can take place."
